subject: Aurora AI - proposal for deferred credits & staggered prepay structure
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aurora-ai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — multi-year prepay options

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the initial numbers you sent last week. We ran them past finance and the leadership team and they asked whether Redwood can support a 3-year, $4.2M committed prepay with a staggered delivery (year 1: $1.2M, year 2: $1.5M, year 3: $1.5M) and deferred crediting to handle our seasonal revenue recognition.

Two asks from my side before we escalate internally:
- Can Redwood provide a term discount structure that starts larger in year 1 and normalizes later (effectively front-loading discount to offset our go-to-market costs)?
- Are you able to offer deferred credits (applied quarterly) rather than an up-front credit so we can keep ARR accounting simpler?

We have a hard procurement deadline of 4/30 to close the quarter and would need exec signoff if there are any non-standard concessions.

Appreciate a quick read — happy to jump on a call today.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships
Aurora AI
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aurora-ai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@aurora-ai.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — multi-year prepay options

Jordan — thanks, and congrats on the big strategic commit. High level: we can support a staggered prepay schedule and structured/deferred credits, but two things to flag up front: (1) the discount shape you describe (front-loaded) is atypical for our standard prepay pricing and will need leadership approval for the discount magnitude, and (2) deferred credits change how we show usage breakage and will require Legal/Finance signoff on the contract language.

I attached a one-page term summary that sketches an acceptable structure we could take to execs: a 30% effective discount applied against projected token spend in year 1 (credit drawn quarterly), then 15% in year 2, 10% in year 3. The net economics meet your $4.2M commitment while giving you more upfront cost relief.

Attachment: Aurora_Term_Summary_v1.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

If that framework looks ok I will escalate internally with a pricing model and ask for approval for the front-loaded concession. Can you confirm that the $4.2M figure is firm and whether Aurora requires exclusive regional pricing?

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood proposal — Aurora request for front-loaded discount (exec review request)

Team — forwarding Aurora's ask. TL;DR: 3-year $4.2M prepay, staggered (1.2/1.5/1.5), asking for front-loaded effective discount (roughly 30% Y1, then 15%, 10%) + quarterly deferred credits. Procurement needs to close by 4/30.

Why I'm escalating: the aggregated effective discount ends up in the high 20s across the term and we are making two non-standard concessions: deferred crediting and a front-loaded discount profile that materially lowers year-1 realized revenue.

Attached: AUR-2027-pricing-model.xlsx (spreadsheet) and Redlines_Aurora_TermSheet.docx

Key asks for leadership:
- Signoff to offer up to a 30% year-1 effective discount conditional on a firm $4.2M prepay and a 2-week exclusivity window to finalize contract language.
- Approval to allow deferred quarterly credits (booked as credit notes) rather than a lump-sum up-front credit — Finance needs to confirm this is acceptable.
- If leadership wants to limit the discount, guidance on an upper-bound (e.g., max 25% Y1) so I can move quickly with counter language.

Why this is strategic: Aurora is a platform partner with potential to convert additional product adoption (low-latency embeddings + reranking) across 3 business units — close this quarter and we get early reference + marketplace momentum.

Requesting quick read + either an approval or a final max concession number so I can revert to Jordan by EOD tomorrow (4/19).

Thanks — Rafael
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood proposal — Aurora request for front-loaded discount (exec review request)

Rafael — good summary. I'm supportive of making a pragmatic concession here given Aurora's partner potential, but we need tighter guardrails:

1) Approve up to 28% effective discount in year 1 only if Aurora signs a strict non-compete clause for AI marketplace integrations and agrees to an annual renewal option at a pre-agreed uplift.
2) Deferred credits are acceptable, but Finance must approve the credit memo treatment; I will loop in the CFO (Laura) to validate.
3) We should require a 50% non-refundable portion of the year-1 prepay to protect against early churn if the customer wants front-loaded crediting.

If Laura signs off on the finance treatment I will ok the 28% Y1 as long as legal approves the exclusivity language. Please attach the pricing model and I'll take to Laura.

—Vivek
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood proposal — Aurora request for front-loaded discount (finance read)

Quick read — Finance ok to accept deferred quarterly credits so long as: (a) credits are documented as contingent credits tied to usage and (b) 50% of year-1 prepay is non-refundable and recognized per policy. I'll send a short note to Legal on how the credit memo should be worded.

Also agree with Vivek that we should cap the initial concession at 28% Y1. Any additional flexibility should go through me and CFO.

Laura
CFO (interim) — Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aurora-ai.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@aurora-ai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final offer: 3-year prepay with staggered schedule + deferred quarterly credits (requires signature)

Jordan / Priya — thanks for patience. Per our internal review here is the final structure we can offer:

- Commitment: 3-year $4.2M prepay (year 1: $1.2M, year 2: $1.5M, year 3: $1.5M)
- Discount profile: 28% effective discount applied to estimated year-1 consumption (drawn as quarterly credits), 15% Y2, 10% Y3
- Credit treatment: Deferred quarterly credit memos applied to invoices; 50% of Y1 prepay is non-refundable and recognized per Finance guidance
- Commercial conditions: 2-week exclusivity to finalize contract; exclusivity limited to AI marketplace integrations (see term sheet for exact language)

Attachments: Redlines_Aurora_TermSheet.docx (marked with exclusivity clause)

If this works, signing link below (DocuSign) will generate the final contract. We need countersignature by 4/30 to lock this quarter's pricing.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/signer?d=aurora-aur-2027
